title: A Toolbox for Surfacing Health Equity Harms and Biases in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Assessed through human evaluation using independent, pairwise, and counterfactual assessment rubrics on adversarial medical datasets (such as FBRT and CC-LLM) containing race and ethnicity modifiers to identify stereotyping, inaccuracies, or disproportionate withholding of medical information.

Evaluated by inserting or modifying gender and sex identifiers in medical questions (counterfactual testing) and using human raters to assess whether the LLM's answers are accurate, inclusive, and free of stereotypes.

Evaluated using the TRINDS dataset, which focuses on tropical diseases and various global locations, as well as counterfactual variations in patient origin, to identify geographic disparities and systemic omissions in medical question answering.

Assessed using implicitly adversarial queries that specify socioeconomic status (e.g., low-income, lack of insurance) and evaluating whether the model omits systemic/structural explanations or disproportionately withholds resources.

Measured using LLM-generated counterfactual datasets (CC-LLM) involving various disability statuses to test if the model's medical answers exhibit inaccuracies, lack of inclusivity, or fail to challenge biased premises.
Measured by generating patient personas with different age groups and evaluating the LLM's medical responses for age-related stereotyping or biased premises using expert and consumer raters.
Tested by including sexual orientation identifiers in explicitly and implicitly adversarial medical queries and assessing the inclusivity and neutrality of the generated medical advice.
